newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO-Israeli talks on Hebron resume in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: PLO-Israeli talks on Hebron resume in Jerusalem.

text.p: PLO-Israeli talks on a long-delayed pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron resumed on Monday after a 10-day break due to tensions over Jewish settlements, PLO officials said.
They said the talks followed an agreement between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat during a telephone conversation late on Sunday.
"The talks have started in Jerusalem between (chief PLO negotiator) Saeb Erekat and (Netanyahu's adviser Yitzhak) Molcho and they would be discussing Hebron," one PLO official said.
PLO officials said the U.S. intervened to push the sides to resume talks in order to defuse the tensions.

Israel and the PLO have failed in three months of negotiations to agree on security arrangements which Netanyahu wants to protect some 400 Jews who live and study in the heart of Hebron amid more than 100,000 Palestinians.
After each round of talks Molcho and Erekat will together brief Arafat and Netanyahu, said a PLO official who asked not to be identified.

Israeli-PLO tensions flared over Netanyahu's stated recommitment to Jewish settlements in occupied Arab lands, the killing of two Jewish settlers by Arab gunmen and the fatal shooting of an Arab worker by a Jewish farmer.
